To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the form of a word can be directly associated with an emotional response; and (2) the use of euphemisms can be explained by the fact that the offending word form is replaced by another word form with a similar meaning.
(1) the phonological form (the way the word sounds) of a word is associated with its affective meaning and (2) this association may be used to control affect and cognition in a top-down manner.

The phonological form of a word can be directly associated with an autonomic response, which is reflected in the fact that autonomic responses are larger to swear words than to euphemistic expressions of the swear words.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how language influences thinking.
the role of language in shaping the way in which people think and feel.
the role of the phonological form in the processing of words.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the findings of this study are in line with the linguistic relativity principle, and that they support the idea that language may have an effect on cognition.
swear words are more arousing and have more negative connotations than euphemisms.
the findings of the present research are in line with a general view of language as a powerful instrument that can influence our thinking and behavior.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the form of a word is a trigger for an affective response and the content of a word is the target of the response.
language is not a mere reflection of the mind but also has a causal role in shaping cognition.
the form of the word, not just the meaning, can have an effect on cognition and affect.
The main takeaway from our work is that
language is not merely a tool to express ideas, it can also influence the ideas we have.
language has a direct impact on cognition, and that the impact is mediated by the form of the word rather than the meaning.
language can influence thinking in a direct and immediate fashion, even in a non-reflective, non-conscious way.
